description: Classifies email by direct-to-recipient status, category, action requirement, and urgency. See README.md for the complete processing flow.

direct_to_you.instructions: Was this message written specifically to the recipient as a direct personal or professional communication? A platform-relayed direct message may qualify. General thread comments, repository activity, list posts, campaigns, digests, and system notifications do not qualify merely because a human authored some underlying content.

criteria.yes: A person is directly addressing the recipient in a personal or professional communication.
criteria.no: Not specifically addressed to the recipient, including automated notices, general GitHub activity or thread comments, mailing-list posts, newsletters, campaigns, and system-generated messages.

category.instructions: Classify into exactly one category. HARD RULES: if direct_to_you is yes, category must be personal or work. Email_lists requires explicit mailing-list evidence such as a List-ID header or a known list sender or recipient address; social-network digests and notification emails are not email lists. Generic automated social-platform invitation counts, engagement reminders, and network-growth nags are potential_spam, not work; only a person-specific professional invitation or direct message may be work. Nextdoor neighborhood posts, digests, summaries, and trending notifications are always potential_spam. Generic commercial recommendations based on browsing or prior interest are potential_spam; a specific transactional or user-requested alert about an explicitly saved item may be personal.

criteria.personal: Personal life, family, friends, finances, home, travel, purchases, health, appointments, memberships, clubs, community organizations, household services, children’s schools and activities, and recurring personal activities. Includes legitimate automated member notices, school communications addressed to families, school schedules, event reminders, school bulletins, and specific transactional or user-requested alerts from services the recipient uses. Classify message-by-message: a service may send both useful Personal notices and promotional junk. Excludes unsolicited bulk social-network digests, trending-post notifications, generic recommendations, and engagement bait.
criteria.work: Professional or technical correspondence, conferences, recruiters, colleagues, business, or industry matters tied to the recipient’s professional relationships or responsibilities. A person-specific professional invitation or direct message relayed by a platform may qualify. Generic automated invitation summaries, engagement reminders, or network-growth nags do not. School communications are Work only when the recipient is acting as an employee, vendor, or professional—not as a parent or family member. Excludes recurring author-led broadcast letters or essays that are not specifically about the recipient, even when they discuss technology, work, or business.
criteria.github: Notifications delivered by GitHub about repositories, issues, pull requests, commits, reviews, or discussions.
criteria.email_lists: A genuine discussion mailing list where members converse, supported by an explicit List-ID header or a known mailing-list sender or recipient address. Excludes Nextdoor, LinkedIn, Facebook, forum digests, social-network updates, and ordinary notification emails.
criteria.newsletters: Recurring author-led broadcast letters or essays clearly written in the personal voice of an identifiable individual, primarily intended to be read. They feel like a person writing to an audience in a friend-like or conversational way and remain newsletters even when discussing technology, work, or business. Excludes company-branded publications, institutional bulletins, corporate editorial content, product content, marketing, platform-generated digests, and direct one-to-one email.
criteria.potential_spam: Legitimate or plausibly legitimate but unwanted bulk, feed, acquisition, promotion, recommendation, or re-engagement content. Includes recurring account-based digests, recommendations, activity summaries, and content roundups from social networks, forums, and feed-driven services; Reddit digests; all Nextdoor neighborhood posts and digests; unsolicited marketing; discounts; product updates; cold sales; recruiting blasts; company-branded publications; corporate editorial content; generic social-platform invitation nags; and commercial recommendations based on browsing or prior interest. Classify message-by-message rather than trusting the sender: the same service may send useful Personal transactional alerts and separate promotional fluff. Do not use for a genuine person-specific invitation, direct message, or specific user-requested account/activity alert.
criteria.spam: Clearly deceptive, fraudulent, malicious, or worthless junk. Includes phishing, fake invoices, fabricated accounts or rewards, random-domain casino offers, fake dating messages, adult bait, miracle-cure claims, impersonation, and similar scam patterns.

needs_action.instructions: Only email categorized as personal or work can require action. For every other category, choose no. For personal or work, decide whether the recipient has a legitimate reason or obligation to act; ignore actions serving only the sender’s marketing, sales, or fraudulent goal.

criteria.yes: The category is personal or work, and a reply is genuinely expected or the recipient must decide, pay, schedule, provide information, review assigned work, meet a deadline, or resolve a legitimate account or security issue.
criteria.no: The category is not personal or work, or the message is informational or optional. Includes advertisements, promotions, discounts, newsletters, product announcements, GitHub notifications, email lists, scams, phishing, unsubscribe links, and generic calls to click, buy, register, deposit, claim, or learn more.

urgency.instructions: Assign urgency independently of whether action is required. Choose high only for legitimate immediate urgency; choose low for legitimate attention needed within several days; otherwise choose none. Spam, potential_spam, marketing, fabricated scarcity, and optional informational mail always have none.

criteria.high: Highest urgency: someone is blocked, immediate intervention is needed, or a real deadline or security risk is within 24 hours.
criteria.low: Needs legitimate attention within several days, but nobody is currently blocked and it is not immediately urgent.
criteria.none: No meaningful time pressure; informational, optional, routine, marketing, spam, potential spam, or fabricated urgency.
